findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments, and no such method exists
findings.body: The only declaration is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160`. A search of the repository finds no overload without arguments in `UsernamePasswordForm`, `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` or anywhere else, so the `services` module will not compile. The call should be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. Even with that fixed, a user who is already set and has no passkey credential would now be shown a username form with the username field hidden (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:100`) when they used to skip straight past it, unless the predicate also checks that the user actually has a passkey (see the finding on `UsernamePasswordForm.java:161`).

findings.title: The `user != null` check turns passkeys off for normal (unidentified) login
findings.body: Before this change, `fillContextForm` ran only when no user was selected: it sat inside the `else` (user == null) branch of `authenticate`, and `challenge` checked `context.getUser() == null`. The new predicate requires `user != null`. So on a first login (`authenticate` line 115, and the error re-render in `challenge` line 137), the conditional-UI and webauthn form data are never set up. Passkeys stay available only during re-authentication, and they disappear from the plain login page. The PR's own tests expect the opposite: `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:196` and `:238` assert that `//form[@id='webauth']` is present on the initial `oauth.openLoginForm()`, where no user is set yet. The likely intent is `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`. That keeps passkeys on the first login, offers them on re-authentication, and hides them for an identified user who has no passkey.

findings.title: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` disables passkeys for the whole realm, so it never tests a user without a passkey
findings.body: The comments (lines 277 and 304) say passkeys should be hidden on re-authentication because this user has no passkey. But the test sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so `isPasskeysEnabled()` is false and the button is hidden for every user. The case that matters is still untested: passkeys enabled in the realm, re-authentication with `prompt=login`, and a user who has only a password. With the current predicate (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:161`) that user would be shown the passkey form, because the predicate only checks `user != null`. Consider running this scenario with passkeys enabled. Also, the try/`fail`/catch(Exception) pattern at lines 291-296 and 312-317 could be replaced with `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`, which the organization test already uses.

contracts.action: Passkey conditional-UI data is set up on the username/password form, now keyed on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: `fillContextForm` was called inside the `else` branch (user == null), and `challenge` checked `context.getUser() == null`
contracts.before_after: Before: passkeys were filled only when no user was set. After: they are filled only when a user is set, which inverts the condition for the first login.
contracts.visible_effect: The webauthn form and conditional UI are missing from the normal login page and present only during re-authentication or after the organization step
contracts.failure_mode: Passkey login silently disappears from the first login; the tests expecting `//form[@id='webauth']` on first load would fail

contracts.action: UsernameForm no longer skips itself for an already-set user when passkeys are enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate for a user who is already set (hidden username, USER_SET_BEFORE note)
contracts.before_after: The no-argument method is undefined, so the code does not compile
contracts.visible_effect: None until it compiles. Once it does, a user who is already set gets a username form with the username hidden

contracts.action: A passkey used during re-authentication (user already set) through the conditional UI authenticator
contracts.equivalent_path: WebAuthnAuthenticator.action, which compares the user handle with context.getUser()
contracts.before_after: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` returns false, so ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS is not set and IS_USER_IDENTIFIED stays false. In action, a passkey belonging to a different user is rejected with DIFFERENT_USER
contracts.visible_effect: On error, `createErrorResponse` re-renders the form with the username hidden and registration disabled, through AuthenticatorUtils
contracts.failure_mode: A passkey for a different user gives an error response with USER_CONFLICT

summary: The PR aims to offer passkeys during re-authentication (for example `prompt=login`), but two defects block it. First, `UsernameForm.java:47` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, and that method does not exist, so the services module will not compile. Second, the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` predicate requires `user != null`, which reverses the old behaviour: passkeys are no longer set up on the normal login page, only during re-authentication. The PR's own tests expect the webauthn form on first login, so they would fail. A likely fix is `user == null || user has a passkey credential`; it would also keep passkeys hidden on re-authentication for a user who has none. The test for that case, `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, turns passkeys off for the whole realm, so it never covers it. The error-path refactor into `AuthenticatorUtils` and the `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` hook look correct, and the existing different-user check still guards passkey re-authentication.
